To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have generated the first genetic map for a parasitic nematodes using genome resequencing data from a single generation cross, and used this to reveal that recombination rates are highly variable across the genome and that there is extensive polyandry in this species.

we have used whole-genome sequencing to generate a genetic linkage map for a noninbred, non-model organism with a complex life cycle and to reveal the recombinaion landscape of the parasite H. contortu.
the genetic map of H. contorus is highly variable, that there is evidence of polyandry and triploidy, and that the genetic map can be generated by resequencing a female F1 and her progeny.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the genetic architecture of the parasitic nematodes, and the mechanisms by which genetic variation is maintained and expressed.
the genetic basis of anthelmintic drug resistance in parasitic nematodes, and the evolution of drug resistance in general.
the genetic architecture of the parasitic nematodes that infect livestock.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study is a significant step forward for the nematode research community.
this study provides a detailed genetic map for a parasitic nematodes that will be of value for future studies in this important pathogen.
we have generated a genetic map for a parasitic nematodes, and have identified the extent of polyadry and polyspermy, and the recombination landscape of the species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have used the first generation of a cross between two diverged strains of H. contortus to generate a chromosome scale genetic map and to identify the recombination landscape of this species.
we have developed a genetic map for the first time in a parasitic nematodes, and we used this map to reveal a highly recombining genome and extensive variation in recombining rates across the genome.

this is the first genetic map for a parasitic nematodes, and the first recombination landscape for any helminths, and it is the first time a genetic map for an outbred organism has been constructed using whole-genome sequence data from a single individual.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recombination landscape of H. contorus, and likely other parasitic nematodes, is highly dynamic.

it is now possible to generate high-resolution genetic maps for any organism, even those with complex lifecycles, and that this can be done using whole-genome data generated from only a single generation of a cross.
it provides a new resource for understanding the genetics and evolution of this parasite.
